Approved by Special Council 25 March 2026 after scrutiny by Corporate Governance & Resources Scrutiny Committee on 19 March. facts.value: Capital expenditure 2024/25 A £38.197m; 2025/26 E £45.985m; 2026/27 E £27.761m; 2027/28 E £26.460m; 2028/29 E £18.647m. Financed largely from grants, receipts, revenue and other sources (£32.802m / £40.622m / £24.471m / £23.654m / £16.241m). facts.note: The CFR includes £1m of finance-lease type OLTL now, rising to £3m by 2028/29 per §3.1 (page 16). Movement built from net financing need plus new finance leases less MRP: -2,422 / -2,819 / -2,616 / -2,644 / -2,905.

facts.value: External Debt (borrowing) 2024/25 A £199.451m → 2025/26 E £204.674m → 2026/27 E £208.380m → 2027/28 E £210.643m → 2028/29 E £214.644m. Other Long-Term Liabilities: £0.685m → £1.947m → £2.410m → £2.773m → £3.036m. Gross debt at 31 March: £200.136m → £206.621m → £210.790m → £213.416m → £217.680m. Actual external debt at 31 March 2026 expected to be approximately £206.6m, comprising 99.9% borrowing and 0.1% other long-term liabilities.

source.title: TSS 2026/27 §3.1 Current Treasury Portfolio Position (page 16) and §3.2.5 Actual External Debt (page 19)

facts.note: The paper does not publish the split of external borrowing between PWLB, market/LOBO and any Welsh Government advances — only the aggregate.

facts.value: Under-borrowing (CFR less gross external debt) 2024/25 A £16.036m → 2025/26 E £13.094m → 2026/27 E £10.600m → 2027/28 E £9.136m → 2028/29 E £5.373m. The Council is deliberately using internal cash balances to fund part of the CFR rather than take external loans, described as a 'deliberate and cost-effective treasury management approach' while borrowing rates remain elevated.

source.title: TSS 2026/27 §3.1 Current Treasury Portfolio Position, page 16

facts.note: Small — never more than about 7.4% of CFR. The gap narrows steadily to 2.4% of CFR by 28/29, implying £10.7m of net external borrowing over four years just to hold the internal position steady.

The dominant single number in the paper: existing loan debt outstanding is forecast to fall by £78.158m in 2026/27 alone (£204.674m → £126.516m) — about 38% of the book cycling off inside this financial year. The (Over)/Under LB row shows the borrowing gap that opens as a result, widening from £2.758m to £100.691m over four years. Paper's own commentary (page 13-14): 'the resulting borrowing gap — the difference between the benchmark and existing loan levels — indicates the level of future borrowing required to maintain an optimal and sustainable funding position.'
Authorised Limit provides £27.8m–£40.2m of headroom over the Operational Boundary, and £22.8m–£33.1m over projected gross debt. Both limits taper from 2026/27 onwards, reflecting the flat CFR.

facts.value: Upper/lower limits on fixed-rate borrowing maturity: Under 12 months 20% / 0%; 12-24 months 20% / 0%; 24 months and within 5 years 50% / 0%; 5 years and within 10 years 75% / 0%; 10 years and above 95% / 5%. Upper limit on fixed rate exposures 100%; upper limit on variable rate exposures 30%; range 70%-100% fixed / 0-30% variable.
facts.note: Limits only — actual maturity ladder in £ terms is not published in this paper, so we cannot check position against limit here. This is a schema gap common across Welsh authorities.

facts.value: MRP on Supported Borrowing: annuity basis over 50 years. MRP on Unsupported Borrowing: Option 3 (asset-life methodology) on an annuity basis, using the weighted average PWLB annuity rate. MRP on Finance Leases: Option 3 modified so MRP equals annual rental. Capital receipts may be used to reduce the overall borrowing requirement rather than making a conventional MRP charge. Loans to third parties: capital receipts from repayments set aside to repay debt in lieu of MRP; prudent MRP kicks in if collateral becomes inadequate or default is likely. Voluntary debt repayment permitted, disclosed in Statement of Accounts; S151 may offset prior-year overpayments against current-year prudent provision. Current MRP policy was agreed by Council in 2021 and remains appropriate.
facts.note: No change to policy for 2026/27. MRP charges built into the CFR movement: -£2.422m / -£2.819m / -£2.616m / -£2.644m / -£2.905m across 2024/25 to 2028/29. Weighted average PWLB annuity rate on unsupported borrowing is a live rate we publish; it is what §3.10 style narratives at other councils have keyed off.

facts.value: Ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream, General Fund: 2024/25 A 3.67%; 2025/26 E 3.81%; 2026/27 E 3.89%; 2027/28 E 3.81%; 2028/29 E 3.69%. Peaks in 2026/27.
facts.note: General Fund line only — no HRA line published, which is unusual for a Welsh authority with council housing. Assumptions: RSG & NNDR up 4.9% for 2026/27 then 3% thereafter; Council Tax up 3.75% for 2026/27 then 4.95% thereafter; Council Tax Base flat.

facts.value: MUFG Corporate Markets forecast dated 6 March 2026. Bank Rate NOW 3.75%, Mar-26 3.75%, Jun-26 3.50%, Sep-26 3.25%, Dec-26 3.25%, then held at 3.25% through to Mar-29. PWLB certainty forecasts (gilt+80bp): 5yr 4.75 NOW → 4.60 Mar-26 → 4.50 Sep-26 → 4.10 by Mar-27; 10yr 5.31 → 5.20 → 4.90 → 4.80; 25yr 5.96 → 5.80 → 5.60 → 5.40; 50yr 5.77 → 5.60 → 5.40 → 5.20. Current PWLB certainty rates as at 06.03.26 a.m.: 5yr 4.84; 10yr 5.38; 25yr 6.00; 50yr 5.82. MUFG target borrowing rate (end Q4 2027): 5yr 4.10 (was 4.20); 10yr 4.70; 25yr 5.30; 50yr 5.10. MUFG note that the neutral long-term Bank Rate remains 3.5% and that better value is at the shorter end of the curve (<5yr PWLB maturity / <10yr PWLB EIP).

source.title: TSS 2026/27 §3.3 Prospects for Interest Rates, pages 20-22

facts.note: Rates have moved AGAINST the forecast between 6 March 2026 and today (16 August 2026). PWLB certainty at 14 August 2026: 5yr 5.34, 10yr 5.83, 25yr 6.46, 50yr 6.27 — 45-50bp above the paper's own 06.03.26 snapshot at every point; also 113-124bp above MUFG's end-Q4-2027 target rates. Bank Rate is still 3.75% — not the 3.50% MUFG expected by June 2026.

facts.value: Under-borrowed position to be maintained. Short-term borrowing remains attractively priced relative to PWLB and provides flexibility while the future rate path is uncertain. Authority will keep under review the option of switching part of its short-term borrowing into medium-term PWLB — up to five years — where this improves cost certainty. Sensitivities noted: if a sharp FALL in borrowing rates is felt significant, borrowing will be postponed; if a sharper RISE than forecast is felt significant, fixed rate funding will be drawn while rates are lower than projected. Debt rescheduling: switching from long to short may still generate savings but must be weighed against premium size, short-term nature and refinancing cost.

source.title: TSS 2026/27 §3.4 Borrowing Strategy and §3.6 Debt Rescheduling, pages 23-25

facts.note: Strategy is a general framework, not a scheduled programme. Cost of carry (higher borrowing cost vs lower investment return) is called out as a live management issue. Section 3.7 confirms usable capital receipts are invested internally, reducing external borrowing needs.

facts.value: Investment priorities: security, liquidity, yield (in that order). Budgeted investment earnings: 2025/26 residual 3.80%; 2026/27 3.40%; 2027/28-2028/29 3.30%; 2029/30 3.50%. Long-term investment limit £50m. Per-institution limit £15m (excluding UK Government). Non-UK counterparties require minimum AAA sovereign rating and £6m per institution cap. Banks - high quality (AAA/Aa2/AA + F1+/P-1/A-1+) £15m for 3 years; medium (A-/A3/A- + F1/P-1/A-1) £6m for 2 years; part-nationalised £4m for 2 years; Barclays (own bank) £10m overnight sweep only, F1/P-1/A-1 minimum; DMADF unlimited for 6 months; corporate bonds AA/A £10m for 4 years; LA per-authority £10m for 3 years; AAA MMFs £10m liquid.
facts.note: Actual investment balances not disclosed in this strategy paper; would appear in mid-year and outturn reports. Advisers MUFG (formerly Link Group) provide the creditworthiness model.

summary.text:
Small Welsh unitary, tight book, no HRA line published. External debt at 31 March 2025 was £199.451m against a CFR of £216.172m — the Council carries £16.036m of internal borrowing and plans to run that down to £5.373m by 2028/29 rather than expand it. The identity CFR − external debt − OLTL = internal ties on every one of the five rows of §3.1 to the pound; the CFR movement built from net financing need plus finance leases less MRP reconciles too (with one page-10 vs page-11 disclosure quirk on the 2024/25 net financing need that's cosmetic, not real).

The dominant single number in the paper is on page 13. Existing Loan Debt Outstanding is forecast to fall from £204.674m at 31 March 2026 to £126.516m at 31 March 2027 — a drop of £78.158m, about 38% of the book, inside the 2026/27 financial year. The (Over)/Under Liability Benchmark row shows the borrowing gap that opens as a result: £2.758m today, £81.090m by March 2027, £100.691m by March 2029. Table §3.1 shows they plan to replace it — Debt forecast to be £208.380m at 31 March 2027 against the £126.516m the LB roll assumes — meaning ~£82m of gross new borrowing scheduled in the current financial year. The paper's own commentary on page 13-14 says the gap 'indicates the level of future borrowing required to maintain an optimal and sustainable funding position'.

Our PWLB file holds 17 loans for Blaenau Gwent at £61.254m weighted 4.3987%. The paper does not publish the PWLB share of external debt, so no direct tie-to-a-printed-table reconciliation is possible — the balance-sheet identity above is what stands in for it. Against the £199m external total, our £61m PWLB implies ~£138m of non-PWLB (short-term LA-to-LA, market loans, or Welsh Government advances). Only £11.2m of our PWLB book matures inside 12 months, so the £78m 2026/27 roll is overwhelmingly non-PWLB.

The paper was written on the MUFG forecast dated 6 March 2026: Bank Rate to 3.50% in Q2 2026 and 3.25% by Q4; PWLB certainty rates already at 4.84%/5.38%/6.00%/5.82% for 5/10/25/50-year on that day. Rates have moved against every point of that forecast since. Bank Rate is still 3.75% (not 3.50%); on 14 August 2026 certainty rates are 5.34%/5.83%/6.46%/6.27% — 45-50bp above the paper's own snapshot at every point, and 100-125bp above MUFG's end-Q4-2027 target rates. That is the context the £82m of 2026/27 borrowing will be raised into.

Break costs on the live book today (16 loans, £58.6m outstanding, DMO 314/26 PM curve) show a net £4.958m discount — 8.5% of principal, 4 loans below par against 12 above. The four big discounts are all on 25-40 year loans at 2.39%-4.25% coupons — cheap money that the discount only crystallises against replacement cost, which we don't model. §3.6 already sets out the rescheduling framework and this note takes no position on whether anything should be done.

No officer name or email address appears anywhere in the paper. The Strategic Director of Corporate Resources (S151) submitted it, and signed off on 17 March 2026, but is not named. So the draft below is written and machine-checked but the recipient line is blank.

officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on the Treasury Strategy Statement that Special Council approved on 25 March. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The paper reconciles cleanly on the identity we always run first, and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

A cross-check first. Every row of your §3.1 Current Treasury Portfolio Position ties on the identity CFR − external debt − OLTL = internal borrowing: £16.036m in 2024/25, then £13.094m, £10.600m, £9.136m, £5.373m out to 2028/29 — to the pound in each year. On the PWLB side we hold 17 loans for Blaenau Gwent at a weighted 4.40% for a principal of £61.25m; the paper doesn't publish the PWLB share of external debt separately so there is no line to reconcile against, but the identity above is what proves the reading was real.

The dominant number in the paper is on page 13. Existing Loan Debt Outstanding is forecast to fall from £204.674m at 31 March 2026 to £126.516m at 31 March 2027 — a drop of £78.158m, about 38% of the book, inside the current financial year. The (Over)/Under Liability Benchmark row shows the borrowing gap that opens as a result: £2.758m at March 2026, £81.090m at March 2027, £100.691m by March 2029. Table §3.1 holds Debt at £208.380m through 2026/27, so roughly £82m of gross new borrowing lands inside this financial year. Our file shows only £11.2m of your PWLB maturing inside 12 months, so most of the roll is non-PWLB — short-term LA-to-LA, market loans, or Welsh Government advances — which we don't hold. The LA-to-LA side of that market is one of the pages we publish daily.

Since the paper was written the market has moved against the MUFG forecast it is built on. MUFG's 6 March 2026 view had Bank Rate falling to 3.50% in Q2 2026 and 3.25% by Q4; the certainty curve on that day was 4.84% / 5.38% / 6.00% / 5.82% at 5/10/25/50 years. Today Bank Rate is still 3.75%, and on 14 August the certainty curve is 5.34% / 5.83% / 6.46% / 6.27% — every point 45-50bp above your own snapshot, and 113-124bp above the target rates MUFG set for end Q4 2027. For context, July sector PWLB lending was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%; the breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

One small anchor from the book we do hold. Four of your loans sit long — PW508742 to 2069 at 2.39%, PW493077/8/9 out to 2053-2057 at 4.25% — and on the DMO's 14 August curve they price about £5.2m below par between them. That's a live break-cost picture with a different answer on different days rather than a case for anything; §3.6 already sets out the framework for a rescheduling decision, and only the DMO can give a binding quote. We model no MRP or accounting treatment. The whole book priced daily is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

On training, five courses sit close to what the strategy commits to. Strategic PWLB borrowing goes to the £82m of 2026/27 borrowing and how it might be sequenced. Liquidity & cashflow forecasting matters given the internal-cash approach in §3.4 and the cost-of-carry note at the end of §3.3. PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator sits behind the discussion above. Working with treasury advisers is where the March forecast question best belongs. Prudential Code and treasury indicators covers the maturity-limit and variable-rate-exposure indicators §3.2 sets but doesn't fill with £-value positions. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
